title: Characterizing CO Emitters in the SSA22-AzTEC26 Field
question: Characterize the physical properties and molecular gas content of four serendipitous CO emitters detected in a blind line search around the SMG SSA22-AzTEC26.

data.bands: Band 3, Band 4, Band 7 (3 mm, 2 mm, 860 um)
data.sensitivity: Band 3 cube: 0.06-0.18 mJy/beam; Band 4 cube: 0.05-0.09 mJy/beam; Band 7 continuum: 0.09 mJy/beam

what.value: Positions of 1.1 mm continuum sources detected by ALMA in the SSA22 field used for astrometry correction

evidence.quote: The astrometry is corrected by stacking cutout images at the positions of 1.1 mm continuum sources detected by ALMA in the SSA22 field (B. Hatsukade, private communication) and fitting a 2D circular Gaussian profile to the stacked image

what.value: Multiwavelength images from u to PLW bands in the SSA22 field

recipe.goal: Reduce ALMA data and create spectral cubes and continuum images
recipe.method: Calibrate and image Band 3, 4, and 7 data using CASA tclean with natural weighting and 100 km s^-1 channel width.
key_parameters: natural weighting; channel width = 100 km s^-1; minimum PB response = 20%

recipe.goal: Blind search for emission line sources and measure line and continuum fluxes
recipe.method: Smooth Band 3 cube with 300 km s^-1 FWHM Gaussian filter, mask central SMG, detect positive and negative peaks above S/N = 1.5 with DAOStarFinder, evaluate purity to set S/N > 5.2 threshold, fit 1D Gaussian to spectra and 2D Gaussian to moment-0 maps.
key_parameters: Gaussian filter FWHM = 300 km s^-1; detection threshold S/N > 5.2 (purity = 83%, a = 4.72, b = 0.71); moment-0 integration range = +/- FWHM from line center

recipe.goal: Extract multiwavelength optical, NIR, MIR, and FIR photometry and deblend source 4
recipe.method: Correct astrometry by stacking at 1.1 mm ALMA positions; measure 2'' aperture photometry in u-to-K with PSFEx aperture correction; deblend source 4 and two neighboring clumps with 2D Sersic modeling in dynesty; perform iterative point-source decomposition for IRAC and prior-based PSF fitting for MIPS and SPIRE.
key_parameters: Optical/NIR aperture diameter = 2''; 1000 random blank apertures for error; Sersic priors n in [0, 6], Re in [0.1, 5 a_image] pixels (pixel size 0.2''); IRAC association radius = 1''
assumptions: Schlegel et al. (1998) dust map and Cardelli et al. (1989) Milky Way extinction curve; two blue neighboring sources near source 4 treated as foreground galaxies.

recipe.goal: Determine photometric redshifts, identify spectral lines, and fit UV-to-FIR SEDs
recipe.method: Model UV-to-FIR SEDs using Prospector methodology implemented with CIGALE models and EAZY to get photometric redshift PDFs, match with candidate CO/[CI] transitions to get spectroscopic redshifts, then refit SEDs at fixed z_CO including ALMA continuum fluxes.
key_parameters: Flat priors: beta in [-0.7, 0.4], E(B-V) in [0, 10], redshift z in [0, 8]; SFR averaged over past 30 Myr
assumptions: Chabrier (2003) IMF; Planck 2018 cosmology; two Noll et al. (2009) / Calzetti et al. (2000) modified dust attenuation curves with old-star attenuation forced smaller than young-star attenuation; nonparametric SFH.

recipe.goal: Calculate CO and [CI] line luminosities and derive molecular gas masses
recipe.method: Convert velocity-integrated line fluxes to line luminosities L' following Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005), convert excited CO to CO(1-0) using normal SFG excitation ratios, and multiply by alpha_CO (and alpha_[CI] for galaxy 1).
assumptions: Normal SFG CO excitation and conversion factor (also tested SMG-like alpha_CO = 1.36, r_21 = 0.84, r_31 = 0.52, X_CI = 10^-4.2, Q_10 = 0.48).

evidence.quote: Source 1 has another line detection at 157.548 GHz, with $S\Delta v=0.320\pm0.044$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ and FWHM of $683\pm201$ km s$^{-1}$.

score_reason: ALMA project codes, calibrators, spectral setups, line search algorithm, multiwavelength flux tables (Table 1 and Table 2), and SED fitting priors are clearly documented, allowing full reproduction of the line detection, SED modeling, and gas mass calculations once cubes are imaged; however, some tclean parameters and two private-communication ancillary datasets are not publicly provided.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA datasets (2019.1.01102.S and 2021.1.01207.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the blind line search recipe (100 km/s channel cube, natural weighting, 300 km/s Gaussian smoothing, DAOStarFinder at S/N > 5.2) is explicit, the extracted multiwavelength photometry is tabulated in Table 2, and all key results (frequencies, line fluxes, M_star, SFR, M_mol) are quantitative.
